newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Duisenberg says optimistic on EMU progress.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg says optimistic on EMU progress.

text.p: Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg said on Thursday he was optimistic about recent developments concerning Economic and Monetary Union.
"If we take a closer look at recent developments concerning EMU, there is definitely cause for optimism," he told the annual meeting of the Atlantic Pacific Exchange Program in Rotterdam.
"True, there are still important hurdles to take, but on the whole I am optimistic."
Duisenberg, Europe's longest-serving central bank chief, is due to take over as head of the European Monetary Institute (EMI), the fore-runner of the European Central Bank, next July.
"...'euro sentiment' is remarkably more positive than it was a year ago," he said in an address released ahead of delivery.
Outlining the European Central Bank's likely strategy to achieve its stated goal of maintaining price stability, Duisenberg said there were two options -- monetary targeting or inflation targeting.

"In my opinion, even if the ECB were to start off its policies with some form of monetary targeting, it might be wise to formulate some kind of inflation targets, in particular since money demand in the first years of EMU should be interpreted with great care," he said.
Duisenberg reiterated his view that the costs of EMU should be seen as a one-off, whereas the benefits would be permanent.
"In my view, EMU will boost intra-EU trade and job creation. There is no doubt in my mind that the changeover costs will be amply offset by the lasting advantages of the single currency."
But he stressed these benefits would only be reaped if EMU proved itself and the euro became a currency "at least as stable as the Dutch guilder and the deutschemark".
Duisenberg said a proper stability pact to ensure continued budgetary discipline after EMU would definitely contribute to the euro remaining a hard and stable currency.
Details of the pact were currently being worked out, Duisenberg said.

"I expect that at its June 1997 meeting in Amsterdam, which will be hosted by the Nederlandsche (Central) Bank, the European Council will reach full agreement on this most important issue", he predicted.
"I am fully convinced that, as far as the stability of EMU and of the euro is concerned, all the necessary conditions will be met," he added.
